title: Weighted matrix integration by parts in a coordinate domain
statement: Use the fields $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $U\subseteq\mathbf R^m$ be open, $m\geq1$, and $r,s\geq1$. Let $H_E:U\to\operatorname{Mat}_r(\mathbf C)$ and $H_F:U\to\operatorname{Mat}_s(\mathbf C)$ be smooth positive definite Hermitian matrices and $\rho:U\to\mathbf R_{>0}$ smooth. For smooth matrix functions $A_j:U\to\operatorname{Mat}_{s\times r}(\mathbf C)$ and $B$ of the same size, put $Lu=\sum_{j=1}^m A_j\partial_j u+Bu$, where $u:U\to\mathbf C^r$ is smooth and $\partial_j$ is real coordinate differentiation. Write $C^\dagger=\overline C^{\,t}$. Define for smooth $v:U\to\mathbf C^s$ the explicit expression $$Qv=(\rho H_E)^{-1}\left(-\sum_{j=1}^m\partial_j(\rho A_j^\dagger H_Fv)+\rho B^\dagger H_Fv\right).$$ This is a complex-linear differential operator with smooth coefficients of order at most one. Whenever at least one of $u,v$ has compact support contained in $U$, the Lebesgue integrals satisfy $$\int_U (Lu)^\dagger H_Fv\,\rho\,dx=\int_U u^\dagger H_EQv\,\rho\,dx.$$

proof.text: Put $M=\rho H_E$. It is invertible at every point: if $Mz=0$ with $z\ne0$, then $0=z^\dagger Mz=\rho z^\dagger H_Ez>0$, a contradiction; a square complex matrix with zero kernel is invertible. Thus $\det M$ is nowhere zero. Its entries, determinant and adjugate entries are smooth, since the determinant and cofactors are finite sums of products of smooth scalar functions. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-nonzero-complex-reciprocal] to $\det M$. The formula $M^{-1}=(\det M)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(M)$ shows entrywise smoothness of $M^{-1}$. This also justifies the inverse in the displayed definition of $Q$.

proof.text: Set $C_j=\rho A_j^\dagger H_F$ and $D=\rho B^\dagger H_F$, both smooth matrices of size $r\times s$. Real coordinate differentiation commutes with complex conjugation and obeys the product rule, so the definition expands to $$Qv=\sum_j(-M^{-1}C_j)\partial_jv+M^{-1}\left(D-\sum_j\partial_j C_j\right)v.$$ Every displayed coefficient is smooth by step 1 and by entrywise finite sums, products and derivatives of smooth functions. This is explicitly a differential operator of order at most one. All occurrences of $v$ and its derivatives are complex-linear, so $Q(av+bw)=aQv+bQw$ for complex constants $a,b$.

proof.text: Fix $j$ and a component $a\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$. On $U$ put $f=\overline{u_a}$, $g=(C_jv)_a$, and extend each by zero to $\mathbf R^m$. Let $K\subset U$ be the compact closed support of whichever of $u,v$ is compactly supported. If $u$ has support $K$, the extension of $f$ is smooth everywhere: it is smooth on $U$ and identically zero on the open complement of $K$. The extension of $g$ is smooth near the closed support of $f$, which lies in $K\subset U$. Hence $f$ is differentiable on the closed support of $g$ and $g$ on that of $f$. If instead $v$ has support $K$, then $g$ is smooth everywhere with closed support in $K$, while $f$ is smooth near that closed support; the same two differentiability requirements hold. On $U$, derivatives of the extensions are the original coordinate derivatives. In either case $fg$, $(D f\,e_j)g$ and $f(D g\,e_j)$ are the zero extensions of smooth functions on $U$ vanishing off $K$. They are continuous globally: each point is in $U$ or in the open complement of $K$. Their closed supports lie in $K$.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-continuous-compact-support-integrable], all three functions in step 3 are integrable. Apply [lem-sfb-scalar-integrable-integration-by-parts] in direction $e_j$, with precisely the supportwise differentiability verified in step 3. Their zero extensions vanish outside $U$, so global integrals are the integrals over $U$. Reversing its equality gives $$\int_U\overline{\partial_j u_a}(C_jv)_a\,dx=-\int_U\overline{u_a}\,\partial_j(C_jv)_a\,dx.$$ Each scalar summand of $u^\dagger Dv$ is also smooth on $U$ and vanishes off $K$, so its zero extension is continuous with compact support and is integrable by the same cited integrability lemma. Thus all sums of integrals used next are finite sums of integrable functions.

proof.text: Expand matrix products entrywise, sum the equality of step 4 over $a,j$, and add the zero-order terms. Linearity for finite sums of integrable functions gives $$\int_U (Lu)^\dagger H_Fv\,\rho\,dx=\int_U u^\dagger\left(-\sum_j\partial_j(C_jv)+Dv\right)\,dx.$$ By the definition of $Q$, the vector in parentheses is $MQv=\rho H_EQv$. Substitution gives exactly the required right-hand integral. The argument treated either support hypothesis separately in step 3 and requires no global boundedness of the other section, of the coefficients, or of the open domain.

lean.statement: theorem weightedAdjoint_spec {m r s : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hs : 1 ≤ s) (U : Set (Fin m → ℝ)) (hU : IsOpen U) (H_E : (Fin m → ℝ) → Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) ℂ) (H_F : (Fin m → ℝ) → Matrix (Fin s) (Fin s) ℂ) (ρ : (Fin m → ℝ) → ℝ) (A : Fin m → (Fin m → ℝ) → Matrix (Fin s) (Fin r) ℂ) (B : (Fin m → ℝ) → Matrix (Fin s) (Fin r) ℂ) (hE : ∀ i j : Fin r, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun x ↦ H_E x i j) U) (hF : ∀ i j : Fin s, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun x ↦ H_F x i j) U) (hρ : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ ρ U) (hEpos : ∀ x ∈ U, (H_E x).PosDef) (hFpos : ∀ x ∈ U, (H_F x).PosDef) (hρpos : ∀ x ∈ U, 0 < ρ x) (hA : ∀ (j : Fin m) (a : Fin s) (b : Fin r), ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun x ↦ A j x a b) U) (hB : ∀ (a : Fin s) (b : Fin r), ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun x ↦ B x a b) U) : (∃ (C : Fin m → (Fin m → ℝ) → Matrix (Fin r) (Fin s) ℂ) (D : (Fin m → ℝ) → Matrix (Fin r) (Fin s) ℂ), (∀ (j : Fin m) (a : Fin r) (b : Fin s), ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun x ↦ C j x a b) U) ∧ (∀ (a : Fin r) (b : Fin s), ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (fun x ↦ D x a b) U) ∧ ∀ (v : (Fin m → ℝ) → Fin s → ℂ), ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ v U → ∀ x ∈ U, weightedAdjoint H_E H_F ρ A B v x = firstOrder C D v x) ∧ (∀ (a b : ℂ) (v w : (Fin m → ℝ) → Fin s → ℂ), ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ v U → ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ w U → ∀ x ∈ U, weightedAdjoint H_E H_F ρ A B (a • v + b • w) x = a • weightedAdjoint H_E H_F ρ A B v x + b • weightedAdjoint H_E H_F ρ A B w x) ∧ (∀ (u : (Fin m → ℝ) → Fin r → ℂ) (v : (Fin m → ℝ) → Fin s → ℂ), ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ u U → ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ v U → ((∃ K : Set (Fin m → ℝ), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ U ∧ ∀ x ∈ U, x ∉ K → u x = 0) ∨ (∃ K : Set (Fin m → ℝ), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ U ∧ ∀ x ∈ U, x ∉ K → v x = 0)) → (∫ x in U, (∑ i : Fin s, star (firstOrder A B u x i) * ((H_F x).mulVec (v x)) i) * (ρ x : ℂ)) = ∫ x in U, (∑ i : Fin r, star (u x i) * ((H_E x).mulVec (weightedAdjoint H_E H_F ρ A B v x)) i) * (ρ x : ℂ))
